messages:
ida: quick note  starting bring-up for glyph-7b candidate quantized to int4. ran our short-query holdout (<=16 tokens) and recall@1 dropped: fp16=0.79 -> int4=0.61. logging initial artifacts here. cc @noah @priya

noah: ouch. which quantizer and settings did you use? symmetric/asymmetric? per-channel?

ida: used the internal quantize tool (v2) with defaults. command:```
python tools/eval.py --model glyph-7b --mode embed --quantize int4 --per_channel false --calib_samples 2048 --calib_seed 7 --holdout data/short_queries.json --metric recall@1 --batch 32
```

priya: useful. try per_channel=true and also asymmetric scales  that sometimes helps represent small-magnitude weights and output projections. did you fold layernorm?

ida: LN folding was on by default. I spun a run toggling folding off just now. per_channel=true bumped recall to ~0.67. int6 baseline sits at 0.75 (almost parity).

bench-bot: eval artifact: https://bench.internal/exp/glyph-7b-int4/1765467891 (internal)

noah: any batch-size sensitivity? microbatching in the runtime can change activation stats post-quant.

ida: yes  bs=1 -> recall 0.60, bs=32 -> recall 0.65, bs=128 -> recall 0.66. microbatching seems correlated.

priya: that suggests calibration mismatch between the samples used to collect scales and actual runtime microbatches. re-run calibration using microbatch-shaped inputs and increase calib_samples to 8k. also sweep calib seeds.

ida: plan: per_channel true + calib_samples 8000 + seeds [7,13,99,123,777]. orchestration snippet:```
for s in 7 13 99 123 777; do
  python tools/eval.py --model glyph-7b --mode embed --quantize int4 --per_channel true --calib_samples 8000 --calib_seed $s --holdout data/short_queries.json --metric recall@1 --batch 32 | tee logs/seed_$s.txt
done
```

priya: also include ablations: final projection forced fp32 ("--fp32-output-proj true") and LN-fold=false. sometimes last linear rounding kills neighbor alignment.

ida: good call. I'll include those variants. also generating top-5 neighbor diffs for 50 random anchors comparing fp16 vs int4 to quantify swap rates.

noah: please capture per-layer activation histograms and L2 norm drift pre/post-quant. that helps spot a specific layer blowing up.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary glyph-7b-int4 rolled to staging @1765468000 :rocket:

ida: quick raw numbers from early sweep (very preliminary): seed7=0.59, seed13=0.62, seed99=0.61, per_channel(seed7)=0.67, per_channel+fp32proj(seed7)=0.69, int6(seed7)=0.75

priya: those numbers look promising with fp32 projection. if the best int4 configuration can't reach our short-query threshold (we target >=0.74 recall@1), we should gate the rollout: route short queries to fp16 or int6 via policy.

noah: agree. also check UMAP of embeddings: I saw cluster fragmentation in the int4 space on a similar run earlier. if fragment size increases for anchors we lose nearest neighbor stability.

ida: UMAPs incoming. neighbor-swap metric shows ~28% top-1 swap for worst seed, down to ~15% with per-channel+fp32proj.

priya: good diagnostics. once you have the full sweep results, upload a short report and we can decide whether to continue tuning or pause the int4 rollout. if rollback needed, set rollout weight 0 and notify infra.

ida: will run remaining variants now and post consolidated numbers in this thread by EOD. thanks everyone.

noah: :thumbsup:
